# Glue

Manage the Data Catalog, connections and Schema Registry, discover local S3 and DynamoDB schemas, and orchestrate local Python shell ETL jobs and workflows.

**Status: implemented subset.** Operation selection does not imply complete input or behavior parity.

| Contract | Current implementation |
| --- | --- |
| Service ID | `glue` |
| Signing name | `glue` |
| Wire protocol | AWS JSON 1.1 |
| API version | `2017-03-31` |
| Scope | Account and region |
| Execution | Records / local S3 and DynamoDB crawling / optional local Python host execution |
| Selected operations | 94 of 314 in the pinned model |

## Implemented behavior

See the [implemented feature catalogue](catalogue.md#glue) for this service's capabilities.

## Limitations and future work

- Spark (glueetl/gluestreaming) and Ray (glueray) definitions are stored, but StartJobRun explicitly rejects execution because TinyStack has no Spark/Ray runtime.
- Glue Studio and managed production engines are outside the implementation.
- Connection records support JDBC, NETWORK, MONGODB, KAFKA, CUSTOM and MARKETPLACE. Credentials and networking properties are stored as supplied. Live connection testing, VPC networking, credential resolution, connection renaming, and newer authentication and compute-environment override members are unsupported.
- NotifyEvent is absent from the pinned Glue API. Workflow events arrive through same-account, same-Region EventBridge rules with a delivery role and no target input overrides.
- Python scripts use the configured host python3 and its installed packages. The bundled awsglue package covers argument resolution; importing GlueContext, DynamicFrame or Job raises a TinyStack-specific ImportError.
- Python shell execution is enabled only when the selected Lambda executor is local; otherwise runs fail with: Local execution is disabled: select the Lambda local executor (lambda.executor: local) to run Glue Python shell jobs.
- Scripts execute with the TinyStack user privileges; this shares Lambda local execution settings and process-group lifecycle, not a sandbox.
- GetJobBookmark, ResetJobBookmark and Python shell bookmark processing are unsupported. Python shell job starts reject bookmark enable, pause and range arguments.
- A claimed RUNNING process is killed on shutdown; its durable run becomes FAILED with an explicit interrupted-execution error after restart, never silently SUCCEEDED; queued STARTING runs resume.
- Cron supports L and nW in day-of-month and L, weekdayL and weekday#n in day-of-week. Combining extensions with lists or ranges, using L offsets, and replaying missed times are unsupported.
- StartWorkflowRun selects exactly one ON_DEMAND source trigger; scheduled or directly started source triggers also create workflow runs; trigger renaming is unsupported.
- JDBC, MongoDB, Delta, Iceberg and Hudi crawler targets are unsupported. S3 and Catalog target connections and S3 event queues fail if supplied. Catalog targets accept only existing S3-backed tables and cannot be mixed with other target types.
- DynamoDB targets use full paginated scans by default or a sample of at most 100 items with scanAll=false. Read-capacity throttling (scanRate) and incremental folder crawls are unsupported for DynamoDB.
- Grok classification uses a single-line RE2 subset with named field declarations, optional type annotations and custom definitions. Built-ins cover words, whitespace, numbers, hostnames, IPv4, log levels and ISO timestamps. Unknown patterns, recursive definitions and unsupported regex syntax fail validation.
- XML classification requires an unqualified RowTag and parses UTF-8 rows with attributes, nested fields and repeated child elements. Athena does not read DynamoDB, Grok or XML crawler output.
- Crawler Configuration accepts only Version 1.0; grouping overrides including CombineCompatibleSchemas and other configuration keys fail explicitly.
- Custom JSONPath supports $, $[*] and dotted member paths with optional final [*]; other expressions fail explicitly. Athena retains its JSON-lines reader and does not interpret custom JSONPath.
- CSV custom datatype overrides support bigint, double, boolean, string and timestamp; other types fail explicitly. Athena supports double-quoted CSV only.
- Crawler grouping merges identical compatible schemas under a target folder; incompatible schemas sharing one root fail rather than inventing a table location. AWS proprietary probabilistic grouping and header heuristics are approximated.
- Crawler exclusions support *, **, ?, and character classes; brace alternation fails explicitly. ListCrawls supports STATE EQ filters only. Estimated remaining time is unavailable (zero with StillEstimating while running).
- A claimed crawl interrupted by shutdown becomes FAILED on restart with an interruption message. Unclaimed RUNNING crawls resume and STOPPING completes CANCELLED. Catalog writes commit atomically after source reads, so stopped crawls publish no tables.
- Crawl output messages use /aws-glue/crawlers with the crawler name as stream; crawling is available independently of the Python executor.
- Job logs become visible after each attempt finishes. ErrorMessage retains at most the last 8192 bytes of stderr.
- Table history lists the current definition first and preserves monotonically increasing IDs across skipped archives. Deletion is limited to archived versions, and archives are cleaned up synchronously.
- Schema Registry accepts AVRO primitives, primitive unions and flat records. Nested AVRO types, aliases, logical types and PROTOBUF are unsupported.
- JSON Schema Registry compatibility checks support flat objects with required properties, single-type or unconstrained properties, and boolean additionalProperties. Use NONE or DISABLED for more complex draft-07 JSON schemas. Remote schema references are unsupported.
- Schema Registry normalizes JSON whitespace and object key order for definition lookup. Registry and schema deletion is synchronous. Registry and schema updates, checkpoint changes, individual schema version deletion, and metadata removal are unsupported.

These gaps describe current boundaries and possible follow-up slices. The [roadmap](../roadmap/index.md)
separates proposed work from registered functionality; there are no promised release dates.
